record.original_question: The CFKRS recipe gives a conjectural full asymptotic formula for Ik(T). Make this recipe rigorous for the fourth moment, by proving the asymptotic formula for I2(T) with a power-saving error term using the recipe method itself.

evidence.quote: Can the ‘recipe’ be made rigorous in the case of the fourth moment? That is, can we give a new proof of the asymptotic formula with power savings error term for I2 (T ) following the ‘recipe’ method.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\zeta(s)$ denote the Riemann zeta function, and for a positive integer $k$ and real $T>0$ define the $2k$-th moment on the critical line
$$I_k(T)=\int_0^T \left|\zeta\!\left(\tfrac{1}{2}+it\right)\right|^{2k}\,dt.$$
The Conrey–Farmer–Keating–Rubinstein–Snaith (CFKRS) heuristic "recipe" predicts that, for each integer $k\ge 1$,
$$I_k(T)\sim \int_0^T P_k\!\left(\log\tfrac{t}{2\pi}\right)\,dt,$$
where $P_k$ is an explicit polynomial of degree $k^2$ whose coefficients are obtained from the recipe (a procedure that, starting from an approximate functional equation for $\zeta(s)^k\zeta(1-s)^k$, retains only the "diagonal" terms in the resulting multiple sum, applies the conjectural shifted divisor-correlation formula, and discards certain off-diagonal contributions). The recipe in its stated form is non-rigorous because the discarding of off-diagonal terms is not justified.

Problem: Working entirely within the framework of the CFKRS recipe (i.e. without using the known proofs of the fourth-moment asymptotic via different analytic techniques), give a rigorous derivation, valid for $k=2$, of an asymptotic formula of the form
$$I_2(T)=\int_0^T P_2\!\left(\log\tfrac{t}{2\pi}\right)\,dt+O\!\left(T^{1-\delta}\right)$$
for some constant $\delta>0$, where $P_2$ is the explicit degree-$4$ polynomial produced by the recipe. Equivalently, justify rigorously each step of the recipe in the case $k=2$, including the treatment of the off-diagonal contributions, to obtain a power-saving error term.
artifact.category_tag: Moments of the Riemann zeta function
artifact.status_search_result: Asymptotic formulas for the fourth moment of $\zeta(1/2+it)$ with power-saving error terms are known (Ingham, Heath-Brown, Motohashi, and subsequent refinements), but these proofs do not proceed via the CFKRS recipe. Making the recipe itself rigorous — in particular, rigorously controlling the off-diagonal contributions discarded by the recipe — is an explicitly stated open problem; searches did not surface a paper providing such a recipe-based proof with power savings.

status_evidence.title: A note on the fourth power moment of the Riemann zeta-function (Conrey)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the fourth power moment asymptotic of zeta on the critical line.
status_evidence.claim: Power-saving asymptotics for I_2(T) exist, but obtained by methods distinct from the CFKRS recipe.

status_evidence.title: The Fourth Power Moment of the Riemann Zeta Function (Heath-Brown)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the fourth moment asymptotic with error term.
status_evidence.claim: Classical proofs of the fourth moment do not use the CFKRS recipe.
